readPmItems is the safe read pattern every demo in this package reuses, and it already distinguishes a spawn error and a nonzero exit from an empty workspace by reporting each on stderr. It does not distinguish a successful read that returned only part of the workspace. The pm list-all envelope has carried a completeness receipt since 2026.8.15, and .items is taken from it without consulting truncated, has_more, completeness.status or omission_receipt. Under pm-cli 2026.8.14 the same call returned 10 items of a 682-item workspace with truncated true, so every demo rendered 1.5 percent of the data and reported success. Because this package is the template other extensions copy, the pattern it demonstrates propagates: a starter that ignores the receipt teaches every consumer to ignore it.

A truncated or degraded envelope produces no rows plus a stderr line naming the tripped signal and the count-versus-total figures, instead of a partial render that reports success.

Review round 2 (CodeRabbit on PR #58) — three findings adopted, one declined.

ADOPTED (Major) — `readPmItems` returned a bare array, so a failed read and an empty workspace were the same value. Both callers guessed "empty": the demo answered `item_count: 0` and the exporter emitted `[]` with `exported: 0`, each reporting SUCCESS for a read that never happened. Logging the cause to stderr did not help, because a return value is what a caller branches on. It now returns a discriminated `PmReadOutcome` (`{ ok: true, items } | { ok: false, reason }`) and both callers go through `readPmItemsOrFail`, which throws a `CommandError` carrying `EXIT_CODE.GENERIC_FAILURE`. The never-throw contract is preserved where it mattered — at the reader, so activation cannot blow up — while the failure now reaches the exit code. Changing the return type made the compiler enumerate every caller, which is how the two demo/exporter sites were confirmed rather than assumed.

ADOPTED (Major) — a top-level array was returned before completeness validation. An array carries no receipt, so it cannot prove it is the whole workspace, and accepting it left a legacy-shaped partial response as an open bypass around every check the rest of this PR adds. Now refused, naming the unverifiable shape. Two suite tests were stubbing exactly that bypass shape and were updated to real envelopes.

ADOPTED (Major) — `envelope as ListAllEnvelope` asserted version-dependent field types on JSON produced by whichever pm build the user has installed. A cast that turns out to be wrong fails its comparison silently, which for a completeness receipt means reporting "complete" for an answer that never claimed to be. Rewritten onto the existing `isObject`/`readPath` narrow readers; the `ListAllEnvelope` interface is gone. A non-string `completeness.status` is now reported rather than passing through untyped.

DECLINED (Minor) — CodeRabbit asked the CHANGELOG entry to describe the fix rather than the defect. The entry text is not hand-written: `pm-changelog` generates it from the item title, and this line sits under `### Fixed`, where Keep a Changelog's convention is to name the bug that was fixed. Every sibling package does the same (`pm-todos`, `pm-csv`, and 18 others), so rewording here alone would break fleet consistency without improving clarity. Recorded rather than silently ignored.

Two further refusals were added while closing the coverage the new branches opened: a complete envelope whose rows field is not an array, and non-object rows dropped from an otherwise complete envelope.

Review round 3 (Greptile P1 + CodeRabbit on PR #58) — three findings adopted, all three in code added by round 2.

ADOPTED (Greptile P1) — `rows.filter(isObject)` silently dropped a null/scalar/array row and still returned `ok: true`, so a shortened workspace was reported as a successful complete read. This contradicted the premise of the whole change: the receipt had just certified the answer as the WHOLE workspace, so returning fewer rows than it contains is a partial read reported as a complete one — the exact failure this reader exists to refuse, arriving through the row payload instead of through the receipt. Now refused, naming the index and the type of the offending row.

Worth recording honestly: round 2 added a test named "readPmItems drops non-object rows from an otherwise complete envelope" which **codified the defect as intended behaviour**. A green suite was therefore evidence for the bug rather than against it. The test is now inverted to assert the refusal.

ADOPTED (CodeRabbit, Major) — a payload of `null`, `false`, `42` or `"text"` fell through to `{ ok: true, items: [] }`, because `describeListAllIncompleteness` answers `null` for every non-object and `readPath` answers `undefined`, so an unverifiable payload became a successful empty workspace. That is the bare-array fail-open one shape over, and round 2 closed only the array shape. Now refused for every non-object, naming the shape received. Regression test covers `null`, string, number and boolean.

ADOPTED (CodeRabbit) — `resolution`, `expected_result` and `close_reason` all still described the superseded contract ("reports the specific reason on stderr and returns no rows"), which the shipped code no longer does: it returns `{ ok: false, reason }`, writes nothing to stderr, and callers convert that into a `CommandError`. Since the CHANGELOG links to this item, a reader following the link reached the wrong contract. All three fields updated through `pm update` (recorded as an append-only event; no history file edited). The wording also conflated the exact dev pin with the lower-bound peer floor and the manifest minimum — corrected to state the three separately, matching the same correction made on pm-brief and pm-context.

Both new refusals verified non-vacuous by reverting each independently. index.ts at 100% line and branch coverage, release:check green.
